conditions.expected: Inspection and explicit repair of a missing database fail without creating it.
An unrelated database is rejected without changing its ownership, schema or rows.
Old and future schema versions remain unchanged during Doctor and current-schema opens; future versions cannot be migrated by this binary.
Missing, renamed or extra migration records cannot masquerade as a valid current catalog.
Missing tables, renamed columns, removed unique indexes and missing or replaced immutable-event triggers are diagnosed, and ordinary Store opens reject them.
Malformed and truncated database bytes cannot produce a healthy report or an implicit replacement.
A mismatched old catalog is rejected before any new schema or catalog row is committed.
An injected migration SQL failure leaves the original version, catalog, schema and rows intact.
Supported migration retains existing source identities, sessions, claims, checkpoints and event receipts.
A required missing work dependency is identified without rewriting source or projection.
A required edge with an absent origin or target is reported with its identity and cannot be silently discarded.
Orphan sessions and invalid claim bindings remain visible; broken foreign keys disable suggested runtime repairs.
An invalid current branch pointer is diagnosed; an explicit selected repair retains unrelated branch history.
An interrupted save remains diagnosable and never replaces the last valid checkpoint automatically.
Pending and failed source mutations remain visible without replay, source writes or false completion during diagnosis.
Missing or changed selected sources produce explicit findings while retained source fingerprints and projections remain unchanged.
An unavailable manifest cannot hide expired claims or prevent an otherwise valid selected runtime cleanup.
Missing, changed and unregistered artifacts are diagnosed without deleting files or exposing their bodies.
Artifact and source read limits remain explicit and cannot produce a healthy unverified digest or leak fixture contents.
After a confirmed live writer is killed, committed WAL session, checkpoint and event history reopens intact.
A killed writer's uncommitted changes do not survive reopening or alter the last committed runtime state.
Reindexing changed source and rebuilding derived search retains runtime ownership and original receipts.
A fresh database from the same sources recovers source facts but cannot claim to recover absent sessions, checkpoints, events or artifact registrations.
A coherent SQLite backup plus retained artifact files restores original runtime identities and receipts; Doctor and CLI confirm the restored state.
